Creating a sustainable web that protects people, the planet, and prosperity is a part of creating a web that works — for everyone. The web was designed for people, but its technology has ramifications for the environment and wider society. Users are concerned about the impact technology is having on the ecosystem, whether that’s the impact of e-waste, or increased demand on power generation and consumption, or data centers, or the emissions of digital products and services. Organizations also need resilience more than ever. We are discussing ways in which the design, development, and operation of digital products and services can reduce negative impacts on the environment while ensuring that the platform remains a good place for people. We work with individuals, designers and developers, software and hardware vendors and regulators to actively engage with our work and to do their part to make the web more sustainable: a web which is open to all, conserves environmental resources, and supports people and society. How W3C approaches sustainability Develop web sustainability guidelines Measure the sustainability impact of implementations Create resources to assist creators with web sustainability Coordinate with research and development that may impact the future sustainability of the web Support education and outreach on web sustainability Coordinate with horizontal review groups to assess sustainability impact of specifications Tzviya Siegman, Director of Sustainability at W3C talks about what digital sustainability is and provides an overview of the Web Sustainability Guidelines. Developing sustainability work Sustainable Web Interest Group The mission of the Sustainable Web Interest Group is to improve digital sustainability so that the web works better for all people and the planet. A big focus of the group is to develop W3C Web Sustainability Guidelines and their companion Impact Ratings. A complete list of the interest group’s deliverables can be found on its GitHub readme . Web Sustainability Guidelines (WSG) W3C Web Sustainability Guidelines are about building digital products that are better for people, planet, and prosperity. In practice, that means using less data, energy, processing, and hardware; keeping websites simple, fast, accessible, and inclusive; reducing waste and unnecessary third-party services; and making sustainability part of product and business decisions. Abstract Web Sustainability Guidelines ( WSG ) provide actionable recommendations to help digital teams make informed, sustainable decisions. In considering different aspects of work and the web, these guidelines address the planet, people, and prosperity ( PPP ) impacts of digital products and services. They are interdisciplinary and cover artificial intelligence and emerging web technologies. Some guidelines reference existing documents and specifications from W3C and other organizations. This approach highlights the importance of intersectionality and collaboration, rather than reinterpreting established recommendations. While WSG prioritizes web technologies, it can also support broader organizational sustainability efforts. WSG can also serve as a practical bridge to support broader organizational sustainability initiatives and transformation, helping teams apply web-focused guidance to broader environmental, social, and governance efforts. Organizations are encouraged to make sustainability progress over time. Setting realistic goals and tracking progress will help teams achieve lasting web sustainability.
